correctness.rationale: Every face uniquely separates into an original matching M and pendant subset T of uncovered vertices. Toggle the least uncovered leaf to pair all faces in each incomplete fiber; only perfect matchings give critical (k-1)-simplices. An explicit directed cover-relation argument proves global acyclicity, including the augmented empty face. Reduced Morse homotopy gives p(G) spheres of dimension k-1, with a direct n=2 check. The standalone checker reconstructs the pairing and independently computes mod-two homology on 1,114 sample graphs; finite tests are supplemental, not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: For a natural standard construction on every finite simple base graph, the exact homotopy type of a generally high-dimensional graph matching complex is determined solely by a classical but nontrivial graph invariant, the count of perfect matchings. The result both detects the existence of perfect matchings topologically and yields exact torsion-free Betti ranks and a uniform discrete-Morse collapse; this goes beyond generic wedge existence and isolated graph calculations. It covers nonplanar families as well as planar ones.
